technique.summary: Exploit JavaScript prototype pollution to inject properties into Object.prototype, then chain this with a gadget in a JS library or framework to achieve XSS. Prototype pollution occurs when user input is recursively merged into objects without proper sanitization.
steps: Identify merge/extend/clone operations that process user input (URL params, JSON body)
Test for prototype pollution: inject __proto__.testPoll=polluted via URL or JSON
Verify: check if ({}).testPoll === 'polluted' in browser console
Identify XSS gadgets: properties that get used in innerHTML, document.write, eval, or src attributes
Common gadgets: innerHTML via data-* attributes, transport_url in analytics libs, source_url in error handlers
Craft a URL with the pollution payload that chains to an XSS gadget

payloads.notes: Direct innerHTML gadget via URL parameter pollution
JSON body prototype pollution with source_url gadget

bypassTechniques: Use constructor.prototype instead of __proto__ to bypass filters
Use JSON body if URL parameters are filtered
Try nested pollution: __proto__.__proto__ for deeper chains
Look for server-side prototype pollution in Node.js apps (can lead to RCE)
